svg.title: One-to-one matching needs a complete native join
svg.desc: Invented example: independent explanation credits one ion against two nearby peaks; assignment credits it once. A native export must bind arrays, candidates and probabilities before matching, then preserve float32 raw21 semantics and require a refit before a fitted ranking comparison. The invented flow has one win, one loss and one pool miss.

g.text: A matching idea becomes a test through its joins
Original schematic • all peak values and outcomes below are invented
Independent explanation
One ion at 100.007 m/z matches both centroids.
Both weights receive credit from the same ion.
One-to-one assignment
The same ion can receive one observed peak.
Maximum observed weight is credited once.
Seal the actual native state before labels
Same query + ordered candidates + unchanged cleaned arrays + explicit fragment families
Current control probabilities / 31-column float32 features / original per-view scores / reviewed pins
Verify native baseline, then change raw21
Same ion bank / 0.01 Da / zero ppm / same-query max
Keep OLD derived22–24. This is a mixed-feature ablation.
Separate the two ranking comparisons
Feature-only ranks: old explanation vs assignment
Fitted ranks: HOLD until new model + exact feature pins
Invented complete flow: one win + one loss + one pool miss
Execution and alignment controls passed. No real model fit, competition metric or improvement is established.
Missing predictions hold the join. Missing acquisition bounds never become peak-derived windows.
A hash binds a declaration; provenance, rights, exposure and an actual refit still need independent review.
